attributes.description: This dashboard gives an overview of resource costs and forecast

params.markdown:
#### Azure Billing

This dashboard reads **deduplicated** cost data from the `azure_billing.usage_fetches` and `azure_billing.forecast_latest` transform aliases, not from the raw `metrics-azure.billing-*` data stream. The time picker and the controls select **usage days**, and the dashboard opens on the current month. Usage days are UTC days, so set the Kibana time zone (`dateFormat:tz`) to UTC to select exact days.

The Azure billing metricset re-fetches the most recent days on every run, so the raw data stream holds several copies of the same cost row. Elasticsearch transforms shipped with this integration record every fetch and which one is the newest, and the panels count, for every day and subscription, only the rows of the most recent fetch, which matters because Azure keeps revising costs for about 72 hours. The raw data stream is unchanged and remains the system of record.

Every cost is broken down by __currency__, so amounts in different currencies are never added together. When you collect more than one currency, pick one with the __Currency__ control, so that the donut proportions compare amounts in a single currency. The forecast shows each scope's newest forecast from today on; forecasts of overlapping scopes, such as a department and a subscription inside it, are added together.

> The `logs-azure_billing.usage_fetches-*`, `logs-azure_billing.usage_latest_fetch-*` and `logs-azure_billing.latest_forecast-*` transforms must be running for these panels to show data. Check **Stack Management > Transforms** when a panel stays empty.

query.esql:
FROM azure_billing.usage_fetches
| LOOKUP JOIN azure_billing.usage_latest_fetch ON azure.billing.subscription_day
| WHERE azure.billing.fetch_key == latest.azure.billing.fetch_key
| WHERE azure.subscription_id IS NOT NULL AND azure.billing.currency IS NOT NULL
| STATS sum_pretax_cost = SUM(azure.billing.pretax_cost) BY azure.billing.currency, azure.subscription_id
| WHERE sum_pretax_cost > 0
| SORT sum_pretax_cost DESC
| LIMIT 10
| RENAME sum_pretax_cost AS `Total costs`
